description:
The US midterm elections are set to take place on Tuesday, in a vote that could have a major impact on Donald Trump’s presidency. 

Americans will choose members of Congress, which is made up of two parts - the House of Representatives and the Senate. The Democrat Party has high expectations, but are the polls right?  

To go through how the next 48 hours might unfold, Adam is joined from Washington by chief news presenter Caitríona Perry and Stephen Hawkins, global director of research at the pollster More in Common.

description:
BBC Panorama has gained rare access to people inside Iran - telling the inside story of how their lives have been shaped by a year of war and anti-government protests. 

In this episode, we hear from Samira, a mother whose 16-year-old daughter was killed during anti-government protests. Samira fled the country on foot, and now lives abroad in hiding. 

We also hear about the medic who received patients injured by bullets as the regime cracked down on protests. 

Months after the wave of protests swept through the country, what does dissent look like in Iran today? How has the war with the US and Israel affected opposition voices?

Iranian authorities acknowledge that more than 3,000 people were killed in the protests, but claim some were members of the security forces. 

One human rights group, Hrana, however, estimates the number of dead stands at more than 7,000 - most of them protesters.

Ukraine and Russia have both said air alert apps were hacked after fake messages warning of attacks, including nuclear, were sent to users. 

Ukraine's app sent red-level air raid warnings across the country, with additional warnings of radiation, chemical attacks, and street fighting sent to some residents in areas including Kyiv. 

A few hours later, Russian authorities said a similar app was hacked after fake alerts, some of which contained foul language, were triggered.

title: Karl Bushby reunites with mum at home after 28-year journey. #KarlBushby #BBCNews

author: BBC News
description:
British adventurer Karl Bushby has completed his 31,000-mile (50,000 km) journey from South America to Hull in the UK, reuniting with his mother at the family home 28 years after setting off.
 
In November 1998, the former paratrooper, then aged 29, set off from Punta Arenas, Chile, to complete an unbroken path back home, without breaking two self-imposed rules: not to return to the UK until the end of the journey, and not to use transport to advance.
 
Bushby said only about 15 of the 28 years were spent walking, with struggles obtaining visas, the 2007 global economic crash and Covid blamed for delays.

He often retreated to Mexico, where costs are low, between stints.

Under the rules he set for his journey, Bushby could not return to the UK to meet his family.

Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert apps were hit by cyber-attacks, with fake warnings sent to users around the countries.
 
In Kyiv, residents received additional false alerts of radiation hazards, chemical attacks and street fighting, with warnings to not go outside. The air force went on to clarify there was no imminent threat of nuclear war, blaming Russian interference.
 
Later, Russia said a "massive cyber-attack" had affected its app, with the emergency services saying specialists were working to restore it. Moscow did not immediately say who might be behind it.

title: Democrat endorses Republican candidate days before US midterms. #BBCNews

author: BBC News
description:
A Democrat in Michigan has endorsed the Republican candidate in the state's crucial US Senate contest, as a spat with her own party's candidate Abdul El-Sayed escalated just days before the vote.
 
Haley Stevens, a sitting congresswoman who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to El-Sayed, made a surprise appearance alongside the Republican candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday.
 
"I don't belong in Abdul's campaign," she said in a video posted to X shortly after that appearance. "Who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now."
 
The move stunned many of Stevens' fellow Democrats who condemned her decision to break from the party and switch her support just two days before the election, with one calling it a "despicable betrayal".
